in_text_mentions: He was assessed at 6 years of age. On physical examination, facial muscle stiffness appeared to have worsened (Figure 1A): he showed pursed lips, almost completed blepharophimosis, and speaking was very difficult due to oromuscolar involvement. Global hypertrophy was evident and motility was completed but clumsy and limited by stiffness. The Gower sign was positive. Myotonia was not observed, but difficulty in muscle release after maximum contraction of the quadriceps was disclosed. He also presented skeletal deformities such as coxa valga and limitations of joint range of motion. The CK was 8

the following routine evaluation, the patient showed a clinical spontaneous favourable evolution with functional improvement. At the last visit, at the age of 10 years, facial appearance was stable (Figure 1B), but he presented a further functional slight improvement in chewing function and speaking. He underwent surgery for blepharophimosis, without significant improvement. The gait was still characterized by stiffness, but functional limitations were not reported yet. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Frontal facial photo from SJS case report; in-text links Figure 1 to mask-like facie, blepharophimosis, microstomia. B: Profile facial photo from SJS case; in-text attributes facial dysmorphism including mask-like facie and retrognathia to Figure 1. C: Maxillary occlusal intraoral photo of SJS patient; in-text describes very severe upper crowding, constricted maxilla and high-vaulted palate. D: Mandibular occlusal intraoral photo of SJS patient; in-text describes lower arch crowding 6 mm. E: Right occlusion intraoral photo showing severe crowding/malocclusion in SJS patient with mixed dentition and severe crowding. F: Frontal occlusion intraoral photo showing severe crowding in SJS patient described with mixed dentition and severe crowding. G: Left occlusion intraoral photo showing severe crowding/malocclusion in SJS patient.
